- When sentiment is neutral or negative (0.00), model tends to overestimate prices; correct by reducing forecast by 2–5% relative to peak or prior high.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >95), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 3–8% for 3–5 days post-spike.
- In absence of sentiment signals, model exhibits strong mean-reversion bias — forecast should be anchored to recent 7–14 day average, not 30d trend.
- If true outcome shows early sharp decline (e.g., 3–5 days), model often lags; adjust forecast to reflect 1–2 day lag in price drop.
- When sentiment is positive (e.g., >0.25), model tends to overreact — reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum at 1–2% below recent peak.
- For 30d forecasts with no sentiment, model often overestimates by 5–15% in first 5–7 days; apply early correction factor of 0.85–0.90 to initial 5–7 days.
